style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The creation psalm -- Genesis 1 sung as praise, day by day, by someone who had been outdoors. Bless the LORD, O my soul: He is wrapped in light like a robe, He stretches the sky like a tent, He builds His upper rooms on the waters and rides the clouds like a chariot and walks on the wings of the wind. He founded the earth and covered it with the deep, then rebuked the waters and they fled to the places He assigned, behind a boundary they cannot cross. Then the psalm gets specific: springs in the valleys where wild donkeys drink, birds singing in the branches, grass for the cattle, plants for man to farm, wine that gladdens, oil that makes the face shine, bread that steadies the heart. Cedars for the birds to nest in and fir trees for the stork, high mountains for the wild goats, crags for the rock badgers; the moon for seasons, the sun that knows when to set; night for the lions to hunt and day for man to work; the sea with its ships and its Leviathan, whom God made to play. Every creature looks to Him for food in season; He opens His hand and they are satisfied; He hides His face and they panic; He takes back their breath and they die; He sends His Spirit and they are created, and the face of the ground is renewed. It ends with a vow to sing as long as the psalmist lives, and one hard line -- let sinners be consumed off the earth -- because the only thing wrong with the world the psalm has just described is them.

1.text: Bless the LORD, O my soul! O LORD my God, You are very great; You are clothed in splendor and majesty,
1.amp: Bless [barak] the LORD [YHWH], O my soul [nephesh]. O LORD my God [Elohim], You are very [meod] great [gadal]; You are clothed [labash] with honour [hod -- splendor] and majesty [hadar].
1.notes: barakhi naphshi et-YHWH (H1288, H5315, H3068): the same opening as Psalm 103 -- the two psalms are a pair, redemption and creation -- YHWH Elohai gadalta meod (H430, H1431, H3966): You are VERY great; hod ve-hadar labashta (H1935, H1926, H3847): dressed in splendor and majesty, the royal pair of Psalm 45:3, now the Creator's own robe.

2.text: wrapping Yourself in light as in a garment, stretching out the heavens like a tent curtain,
2.amp: You who cover [atah -- wrap] Yourself with light [or] as with a garment [salmah -- mantle]: who stretch out [natah] the heavens [shamayim] like a curtain [yeriah -- tent-curtain]:
2.notes: oteh-or ka-salmah (H5844, H216, H8008): light as the mantle He wraps in -- day one -- noteh shamayim ka-yeriah (H5186, H8064, H3407): the heavens stretched like a tent-curtain, day two. Genesis 1 in participles, the Creator still doing it. yeriah (H3407) is the word for the tabernacle's tent-curtains (Exodus 26:1) -- not yareach, the moon of verse 19.

3.text: laying the beams of His upper rooms on the waters, making the clouds His chariot, walking on the wings of the wind,
3.amp: Who lays the beams [qarah -- frames with beams] of His chambers [aliyyah -- upper rooms] in the waters [mayim]: who makes [sum] the clouds [ab] His chariot [rekub]: who walks [halak] upon the wings [kanaph] of the wind [ruach]:
3.notes: ha-meqareh ba-mayim aliyyotav (H7136, H4325, H5944): the beams of His upper story laid on the waters above the sky -- ha-sam-abim rekhubo (H7760, H5645, H7398): clouds for a chariot -- ha-mehallekh al-kanphe-ruach (H1980, H3671, H7307): walking on the wind's wings, Psalm 18:10's picture. The God of the storm-hymn as the God of the weather report.

4.text: making His messengers winds, His ministers a flaming fire.
4.amp: Who makes [asah] His angels [malak -- messengers] spirits [ruach -- winds]; His ministers [sharath -- attendants] a flaming [lahat] fire [esh]:
4.notes: oseh malakhav ruchot (H6213, H4397, H7307): His messengers made winds -- or His winds made messengers; the Hebrew runs both ways -- mesharetav esh lohet (H8334, H784, H3857): His servants a blazing fire. Hebrews 1:7 quotes the line of the angels, to show the Son is more than they.

5.text: He founded the earth on its bases, so that it will not be shaken, forever and ever.
5.amp: Who laid [yasad] the foundations ['He hath founded the earth upon her bases', makon, the KJV margin] of the earth [eretz], that it should not be removed [mot] for ever [olam] and ever [ad].
5.notes: yasad-eretz al-mekhoneha (H3245, H776, H4349): the margin's literal -- founded the earth on her bases -- bal-timmot olam va-ed (H4131, H5769, H5703): not to totter forever and ever. The earth's fixity, Psalm 93:1's 'cannot be moved' -- day three proper follows in verses 7-9.

6.text: You covered it with the deep as with clothing; the waters stood high above the mountains.
6.amp: You covered [kasah] it with the deep [tehom] as with a garment [lebush]: the waters [mayim] stood [amad] above the mountains [har].
6.notes: tehom ka-lebush kissito (H8415, H3830, H3680): the tehom, Genesis 1:2's deep, worn by the earth like clothing -- al-harim yaamdu-mayim (H2022, H5975, H4325): the waters standing above the mountains. The world before the third day's word.

7.text: At Your rebuke they took flight; at the sound of Your thunder they scrambled away --
7.amp: At [min] Your rebuke [gearah] they fled [nus]; at the voice [qol] of Your thunder [raam] they hasted away [chaphaz].
7.notes: min-gaaratekha yenusun (H4480, H1606, H5127): the waters FLEE at a rebuke -- Psalm 114:3's bolting sea -- min-qol raamkha yechaphezun (H6963, H7482, H2648): at the thunder's voice they scramble. 'Let the waters be gathered' (Genesis 1:9) heard as a shout that the sea obeyed in a panic.

8.text: the mountains rose, the valleys sank down -- to the place You had founded for them.
8.amp: They go up ['The mountains ascend, the valleys descend', the KJV margin] by the mountains [har]; they go down [yarad] by the valleys [biqah -- broad valleys] unto the place [maqom] which [zeh] You have founded [yasad] for them.
8.notes: yaalu harim yerdu beqaot (H5927, H2022, H3381, H1237): the margin's reading, which the WEB follows -- mountains rising, valleys sinking, the land itself moving -- el-meqom zeh yasadta lahem (H4725, H2088, H3245): to the place You founded for them. Either the waters or the landforms are the subject; both end up where they were told.

9.text: You set a boundary they may not cross, so that they will never again cover the earth.
9.amp: You have set [sum] a bound [gebul -- boundary] that they may not pass over [abar]; that they turn not again [shub] to cover [kasah] the earth [eretz].
9.notes: gebul-samta bal-yaaborun (H1366, H7760, H5674): a border the sea may not cross -- Job 38:11's 'hitherto shalt thou come' -- bal-yeshubun le-khassot ha-aretz (H7725, H3680, H776): never again to cover the earth: the rainbow covenant of Genesis 9:11 in the creation hymn.

10.text: He sends springs into the ravines; they run between the mountains,
10.amp: He ['Who', the KJV margin] sends [shalach] the springs [maayan] into the valleys [nachal -- ravines, wadis], which run ['walk', halak, the KJV margin] among the hills [har].
10.notes: ha-meshalleach mayanim ba-nechalim (H7971, H4599, H5158): springs DISPATCHED into the wadis -- ben harim yehallekhun (H2022, H1980): they WALK between the mountains, the margin's verb. The waters that were rebuked in verse 7 are now sent on errands.

11.text: giving drink to every beast of the field; the wild donkeys quench their thirst.
11.amp: They give drink [shaqah] to every beast [chay] of the field [sadeh]: the wild asses [pere] quench ['break', shabar, the KJV margin] their thirst [tsama].
11.notes: yashqu kol-chayto sadai (H8248, H2416, H7704): every living thing of the field watered -- yishberu pheraim tsemaam (H7665, H6501, H6772): the wild donkeys BREAK their thirst, the margin's idiom -- the pere, the untamable ass of Job 39:5, drinking from God's tap. The creation psalm keeps choosing animals no one owns.

12.text: Beside them the birds of the sky make their home; among the branches they give voice.
12.amp: By them shall the fowls [oph] of the heaven [shamayim] have their habitation [shakan], which sing ['give a voice', natan qol, the KJV margin] among [beyn] the branches [ophaim -- foliage].
12.notes: alehem oph-ha-shamayim yishkon (H5775, H8064, H7931): the birds of the sky TABERNACLE by the streams -- mi-ben ophaim yittenu-qol (H996, H6073, H5414, H6963): from between the leaves they give voice, the margin's literal. Birdsong as the fifth day's contribution to the liturgy.

13.text: He waters the mountains from His upper rooms; the earth is satisfied with the fruit of Your works.
13.amp: He waters [shaqah] the hills [har] from His chambers [aliyyah -- upper rooms]: the earth [eretz] is satisfied [saba] with the fruit [peri] of Your works [maaseh].
13.notes: mashqeh harim me-aliyyotav (H8248, H2022, H5944): the mountains watered from the upper rooms of verse 3 -- rain from God's attic -- mi-peri maasekha tisba ha-aretz (H6529, H4639, H7646, H776): the earth SATISFIED with the fruit of Your works. saba, the full-stomach word: the planet fed.

14.text: He makes grass grow for the cattle, and plants for man to cultivate, to bring bread out of the earth,
14.amp: He causes the grass [chatsir] to grow [tsamach -- sprout] for the cattle [behemah], and herb [eseb -- plants] for the service [abodah -- labor, cultivation] of man [adam]: that he may bring forth [yatsa] food [lechem -- bread] out of the earth [eretz];
14.notes: matsmiach chatsir la-behemah (H6779, H2682, H929): grass sprouted for the livestock -- ve-eseb la-abodat ha-adam (H6212, H5656, H120): and plants for man's LABOR -- agriculture as a joint venture: God grows, man works -- le-hotsi lechem min-ha-aretz (H3318, H3899, H776): to bring bread out of the ground. Genesis 3:19's sweat, sung as a gift.

15.text: and wine that makes the heart of man glad, oil to make his face shine, and bread that steadies the heart of man.
15.amp: And wine [yayin] that makes glad [samach] the heart [lebab] of man [enosh], and oil [shemen] to make his face [panim] to shine ['to make his face shine with oil, or, more than oil', the KJV margin], and bread [lechem] which strengthens [saad -- sustains] man's heart.
15.notes: ve-yayin yesammach lebab-enosh (H3196, H8055, H3824, H582): wine that gladdens -- the psalm's unembarrassed word for it -- le-hatshil panim mi-shamen (H6670, H6440, H8081): oil for a shining face, the ancient world's cosmetic and comfort -- ve-lechem lebab-enosh yisad (H3899, H5582): bread that props the heart up. Three staples of a Mediterranean table, all of them from God's hand (cf. Judges 9:13; Ecclesiastes 9:7).

16.text: The trees of the LORD are satisfied, the cedars of Lebanon that He Himself planted,
16.amp: The trees [ets] of the LORD [YHWH] are full [saba -- satisfied] of sap; the cedars [erez] of Lebanon [Lebanon], which He has planted [nata];
16.notes: yisbeu atse YHWH (H7646, H6086, H3068): the LORD's own trees, satisfied -- arze Lebanon asher nata (H730, H3844, H5193): the cedars He PLANTED. No one planted the cedars of Lebanon; the psalm says Someone did. The wild forest as God's orchard.

17.text: where the birds build their nests; as for the stork, the fir trees are her house.
17.amp: Where the birds [tsippor] make their nests [qanan]: as for the stork [chasidah], the fir trees [berosh -- cypresses] are her house [bayith].
17.notes: asher-sham tsipporim yeqannenu (H6833, H7077): where the birds nest -- chasidah beroshim betah (H2624, H1265, H1004): the stork -- chasidah, traditionally read as 'the kind one' (from chesed) for the stork's reputed devotion to its young -- housed in the cypress. Even the nesting arrangements are in the inventory.

18.text: The high mountains are for the wild goats; the crags are a refuge for the rock badgers.
18.amp: The high [gaboah] hills [har] are a refuge [machseh] for the wild goats [yael -- ibex]; and the rocks [sela -- crags] for the conies [shaphan -- rock badgers].
18.notes: harim ha-gebohim la-yeelim (H2022, H1364, H3277): the high mountains for the ibex -- selaim machseh la-shephannim (H5553, H4268, H8227): the crags a refuge for the shephannim, the rock hyrax, Proverbs 30:26's 'feeble folk' who live in the rocks. The Creator assigned habitats; the psalm's zoology is Judean.

19.text: He made the moon to mark the appointed times; the sun knows the place of its setting.
19.amp: He appointed [asah -- made] the moon [yareach] for seasons [moed -- appointed times]: the sun [shemesh] knows [yada] his going down [mabo].
19.notes: asah yareach le-moadim (H6213, H3394, H4150): the moon made for MOADIM -- the appointed feasts, dated by the new moons of a lunisolar calendar -- shemesh yada meboo (H8121, H3045, H3996): the sun KNOWS its setting-place; day four's lights given a job and, poetically, a mind.

20.text: You bring darkness, and it is night, when all the beasts of the forest come creeping out.
20.amp: You make [shith] darkness [choshek], and it is night [layil]: wherein all the beasts ['beasts thereof do trample on the forest', chay, the KJV margin] of the forest [yaar] do creep [ramas -- prowl] forth.
20.notes: tashet-choshekh vi-hi lailah (H7896, H2822, H3915): You SET darkness and it becomes night -- darkness as a thing God places, not an absence -- bo-tirmos kol-chayto-yaar (H7430, H2416, H3293): in it every forest beast prowls. The night shift of creation begins.

21.text: The young lions roar after their prey, and so they seek their food from God.
21.amp: The young lions [kephir] roar [shaag] after their prey [tereph], and seek [baqash] their meat [okel -- food] from God [El].
21.notes: ha-kephirim shoagim la-tareph (H3715, H7580, H2964): the lions' roar -- u-le-baqqesh me-El okhlam (H1245, H410, H400): and to SEEK from God their food. The roar is a prayer; the predator is a dependent. Psalm 147:9's ravens, in a larger throat.

22.text: The sun rises; they gather themselves and lie down in their dens.
22.amp: The sun [shemesh] arises [zarach], they gather themselves together [asaph], and lay them down [rabats] in their dens [meonah].
22.notes: tizrach ha-shemesh yeasephun (H2224, H8121, H622): sunrise, and the lions collect themselves -- ve-el-meonotam yirbatsun (H4585, H7257): and lie down in their lairs, the shepherd's word for flocks at rest. Night creatures clock out.

23.text: And man goes out to his work, and stays at his labor till evening falls.
23.amp: Man [adam] goes forth [yatsa] unto his work [poal] and to his labour [abodah] until the evening [erev].
23.notes: yetse adam le-phoolo (H3318, H120, H6467): and man clocks in -- ve-la-abodato ade-arev (H5656, H6153): to his labor until evening. The same abodah as verse 14's cultivation: the shift system of creation, lions by night, men by day, one Provider for both.

24.text: How many are Your works, O LORD! In wisdom You have made them all; the earth is full of what You own.
24.amp: O LORD [YHWH], how manifold [rabab -- many] are Your works [maaseh]! in wisdom [chokmah] have You made [asah] them all: the earth [eretz] is full [male] of Your riches [qinyan -- possessions, creatures].
24.notes: mah-rabbu maasekha YHWH (H7231, H4639, H3068): how MANY Your works -- the psalm's exclamation halfway through the tour -- kullam be-chokhmah asita (H2451, H6213): all of them made in wisdom, Proverbs 8:22-31's Wisdom at the Creator's side -- maleah ha-aretz qinyanekha (H4390, H776, H7075): the earth full of Your qinyan, Your acquisitions -- what You own. Every creature is God's property.

25.text: There is the sea, great and broad, with its swarming things past counting, living creatures small and great.
25.amp: So is this great [gadol] and wide [rachab yad -- broad of hand, spacious] sea [yam], wherein are things creeping [remes -- swarming] innumerable [en mispar], both small [qatan] and great [gadol] beasts [chay].
25.notes: zeh ha-yam gadol u-rechab yadayim (H3220, H1419, H7342, H3027): the sea, great and 'wide of hands', the Hebrew idiom for spaciousness -- sham-remes ve-en mispar (H7431, H4557): swarming things without number -- chayyot qetannot im-gedolot (H2416, H6996, H1419): small creatures with great. Day five's oceans; the psalmist has stood on the shore.

26.text: There the ships travel, and Leviathan, whom You formed to play in it.
26.amp: There go [halak] the ships [oniyyah]: there is that leviathan [Livyatan], whom You have made ['formed', yatsar, the KJV margin] to play [sachaq -- laugh, sport] therein.
26.notes: sham oniyyot yehallekhun (H591, H1980): ships walking the sea -- Livyatan zeh-yatsarta le-sacheq-bo (H3882, H3335, H7832): Leviathan, whom You FORMED to play there. The sea monster of Job 41 and Canaanite myth is, in this psalm, God's pet -- made for sport, not combat. The most disarming line in the Old Testament's theology of chaos.

27.text: All of them look to You to give them their food at the right time.
27.amp: These wait [sabar -- look expectantly] all upon You; that You may give [natan] them their meat [okel -- food] in due season [et].
27.notes: kullam elekha yesabberun (H7663): ALL of them -- lions, storks, Leviathan -- look to You with expectation -- latet okhlam be-itto (H5414, H400, H6256): to give their food in its time. Psalm 145:15's line; creation as a table where every seat faces the Host.

28.text: You give to them; they gather it up. You open Your hand; they are filled with good things.
28.amp: That You give [natan] them they gather [laqat -- glean]: You open [pathach] Your hand [yad], they are filled [saba] with good [tov].
28.notes: titten lahem yilqotun (H5414, H3950): You give, they glean -- the harvest-verb of Ruth -- tiphtach yadekha yisbeun tov (H6605, H3027, H7646, H2896): You open Your hand, they are sated with good. the same open hand as Psalm 145:16, which reworks this line; the open hand is the psalm's picture of providence.

29.text: You hide Your face; they are dismayed. You take back their breath; they die and return to their dust.
29.amp: You hide [satar] Your face [panim], they are troubled [bahal -- dismayed, panicked]: You take away [asaph -- gather in] their breath [ruach], they die [gava -- expire], and return [shub] to their dust [afar].
29.notes: tastir panekha yibbahelun (H5641, H6440, H926): the hidden face means panic -- for animals too -- toseph rucham yigvaun (H622, H7307, H1478): You GATHER IN their breath and they expire -- ve-el-apharam yeshubun (H6083, H7725): back to their dust, Genesis 3:19 for every creature. Life is on loan, breath by breath.

30.text: You send out Your Spirit; they are created, and You renew the face of the ground.
30.amp: You send [shalach] forth Your Spirit [ruach], they are created [bara]: and You renew [chadash] the face [panim] of the earth [adamah -- ground].
30.notes: teshallach ruchakha yibbareun (H7971, H7307, H1254): You send Your ruach -- Spirit, breath -- and they are CREATED, bara, Genesis 1:1's verb, happening every spring -- u-techaddesh pene adamah (H2318, H6440, H127): You renew the face of the ground. The Western church's ancient Pentecost versicle, Emitte Spiritum tuum ('send forth Your Spirit'), is this line: the Spirit who brooded over the deep (Genesis 1:2) is the same Spirit who upholds and renews what He made -- the psalm lends creation's own verb to God's ongoing providence.

31.text: Let the glory of the LORD endure forever; let the LORD take joy in His works.
31.amp: The glory [kabod] of the LORD [YHWH] shall endure ['be', the KJV margin] for ever [olam]: the LORD shall rejoice [samach] in His works [maaseh].
31.notes: yehi khebod YHWH le-olam (H3519, H3068, H5769): let the glory BE forever, the margin's verb -- yismach YHWH be-maasav (H8055, H4639): let the LORD REJOICE in His works. Genesis 1:31's 'very good' as an ongoing delight: God enjoying what He made, and the psalmist praying that He always will.

32.text: One look from Him and the earth trembles; one touch on the mountains and they smoke.
32.amp: He looks [nabat] on the earth [eretz], and it trembles [raad]: He touches [naga] the hills [har], and they smoke [ashan].
32.notes: ha-mabbit la-aretz va-tirad (H5027, H776, H7460): a look, and the earth shudders -- yigga be-harim ve-yeeshanu (H5060, H2022, H6225): a touch, and the mountains smoke -- Sinai (cf. Exodus 19:18) and Psalm 144:5. The God who feeds the lions can also unmake the landscape with a glance; the joy of verse 31 is not sentimentality.

33.text: I will sing to the LORD as long as I live; I will make music to my God while I still have being.
33.amp: I will sing [shir] unto the LORD [YHWH] as long as I live [chay]: I will sing [zamar] praise to my God [Elohim] while I have my being [od -- yet, still].
33.notes: ashirah la-YHWH be-chayyai (H7891, H3068, H2416): song for the length of a life -- azammerah l-Elohai be-odi (H2167, H430, H5750): music while I still AM, Psalm 146:2's vow. The creature that can sing, singing; the psalmist takes his place in the inventory of verses 10-26.

34.text: May my meditation be sweet to Him; as for me, I will rejoice in the LORD.
34.amp: My meditation [siach] of Him shall be sweet [arab -- pleasing]: I will be glad [samach] in the LORD [YHWH].
34.notes: yeerab alav sichi (H6149, H7879): may my musing be sweet TO HIM -- the psalm asks that its own words please God, the way the smoke of an offering does. anokhi esmach ba-YHWH (H8055, H3068): as for me, I will be glad in the LORD -- the creature's joy answering the Creator's (v. 31).

35.text: Let sinners be consumed off the earth, and the wicked exist no more. Bless the LORD, O my soul! Praise the LORD!
35.amp: Let the sinners [chatta] be consumed [tamam -- brought to an end] out of the earth [eretz], and let the wicked [rasha] be no more. Bless [barak] You the LORD [YHWH], O my soul [nephesh]. Praise [halal] ye the LORD [Yah].
35.notes: yittammu chattaim min-ha-aretz (H8552, H2400, H776): the one discordant note -- and the reason for it: after thirty-four verses of a world that works, the only broken part is the sinners, u-reshaim od enam (H7563), 'and the wicked be no more', and the psalmist wants the picture completed. barakhi naphshi et-YHWH (H1288, H5315): the frame of verse 1 closes -- and then the Psalter's FIRST halelu-Yah (H1984, H3050), 'praise Yah': the word makes its debut at the end of the creation psalm.
